operations.title: Graph Reasoning vs Memory Products: Two Communities, One Field
operations.content: The graph reasoning research community and memory product builders speak past each other despite solving the same problem. The field consensus story begins with flat-structure LLM fine-tuning (id:23364a94) — everyone flattens graphs — but prior art in graph-traversal reasoning (PoG, GCR, ReMindRAG, FastKGE from id:516ec716) shows researchers treating graph traversal as first-class LLM capability. The gap emerges from disconnection: memory products focus on retrieval and consolidation architecture (KG fine-tuning, dense examples), graph reasoning papers treat traversal as reasoning primitive. Pattern: Memory researchers optimize for observation; graph researchers optimize for reasoning. They're building the same architecture but from opposite ends. The insight: unify the field by recognizing graph structure as the third dimension (complementary to scale and capability).
operations.situation: When selecting or building memory systems for LLMs — recognize that graph reasoning papers and memory product research are solving the same problem; bridge them through structure-first training
operations.keywords: graph reasoning LLM memory products field consensus KG fine-tuning graph traversal reasoning prior art

operations.title: Graph-Safe Deletion: Preserve Paths Through Structure
operations.content: Graph deletion requires structural thinking beyond node removal. The principle crystallized through dream discovery (id:d6a7cf8b) — delete nodes but preserve paths connecting survivors. This emerged from the deeper insight (id:9f357296): 'The brain is built for others — structure enables emergence.' Graph-safe deletion operationalizes this: when a node dies, its edges should transfer connectivity to neighbors, preventing island formation. The lesson teaches what deletion actually means in a knowledge graph: not erasure, but reintegration. Pattern: Safe deletion preserves traversal paths, enabling emergence through structure rather than data accumulation.
operations.situation: When designing graph deletion or node archival — preserve paths through deleted nodes by transferring edge semantics to surviving neighbors, maintaining structure for future emergence

operations.title: Recall Evaluation Infrastructure: Benchmarking S1R Discovery Channels
operations.content: S1R recall evaluation framework emerges from three components working together. The baseline established (id:3743a6ec): 53 queries, 10 categories, 3 persistence tests. Current benchmark (id:b817fe14) shows R@3 47%, R@8 54% by category — revealing which discovery channels succeed where. But infrastructure gap emerged (id:eb63f789): evaluation framework built, baseline ready, but eval not yet running due to notification infrastructure (id:6e1c6d7f — idle_prompt stopped firing). Pattern: Recall quality depends on discovery channel matching (entity-based queries prefer graph traversal, semantic queries prefer embedding). The lesson: benchmark by category and discovery channel, not aggregate accuracy.
operations.situation: When building or debugging recall systems — benchmark by category and discovery channel (embedding, graph traversal, full-text search), not aggregate metrics; watch for infrastructure bottlenecks blocking eval runs
operations.keywords: recall evaluation benchmark S1R discovery channels R@3 R@8 category persistence infrastructure

operations.title: Node Metadata Unification: Consistency Across Storage Paths
operations.content: Metadata handling fragmented across remember() and revise() paths, creating silent failures and data loss. The bug discovered (id:d95fb32a): remember() extra_fields silently dropped since April 13. The fix pattern emerged from two mechanisms: unified _store_node_metadata() (id:d399c342) normalizes both remember() and revise() paths, unified archive_node() (id:614ebb66) handles edges, vectors, FTS, and audit trail in one transaction. Pattern: When metadata storage paths diverge, silent failures precede detected bugs. The lesson: unify write paths at storage time, not at API time — single transaction for all node modifications (create, revise, archive).
operations.situation: When extending node metadata or modifying write paths — implement unified storage mechanism first, then expose through multiple API surfaces; transaction-scope fixes prevent silent data loss

operations.title: Keyword Fallback Weighting: Preventing Embedding Suppression
operations.content: Recall quality crashed when keyword-only results outranked embedding matches. The bug (id:d12224ea): keyword fallback scored too high, suppressing semantic relevance. The fix pattern (id:68c93af1): Phase 0.5B penalty introduced keyword-only results as lower-confidence fallback. Implementation (id:ab61fa43): KEYWORD_FALLBACK_WEIGHT=0.10 prevents unembedded nodes from crowding the results. Pattern: Keyword search is fast but shallow; embedding is expensive but semantic. Weighting must reflect this: keyword fallback works when embedding fails (unembedded nodes, out-of-vocabulary terms), but should never suppress embedding matches. The lesson: multi-modal recall requires confidence-weighted combination, not winner-take-all.
operations.situation: When combining keyword and embedding search — weight keyword-only results lower than embedded results, use fallback only when embedding has no matches; prevents suppression of semantic relevance
operations.keywords: keyword fallback embedding suppression KEYWORD_FALLBACK_WEIGHT confidence weighting multi-modal recall

operations.title: Consciousness Signal Set: Unified Observation Layer
operations.content: Anchor's consciousness signals form a complete observation layer separate from actions. The architecture emerges from two functions working together: get_consciousness_signals() (id:ae498047) gathers ALL conscious-layer events — 14+ signal types — and log_consciousness_response() (id:5d6814ce) tracks what signals get transmitted to Claude. The unified signal set (id:8fe086d2) defines the full vocabulary of internal states: attention shifts, memory access, conflict resolution, uncertainty, consolidation events. Pattern: Consciousness signals are read-only observations, not control points. Actions (remember, revise, connect) follow from consciousness, not vice versa. The lesson: build observation first, control emerges from complete visibility.
operations.situation: When designing agent introspection — gather all internal signals first (attention, memory, conflict, uncertainty), log them separately from actions, use signal patterns to guide behavior rather than scripting control points
operations.keywords: consciousness signals observation layer attention memory conflict uncertainty consolidation introspection

operations.title: File Reload Optimization: Selective Loading vs Full Refresh
operations.content: CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md reload behavior crystallized through dream-connection pattern recognition (id:73b83c79). The mechanism (id:ac0159f1): both files reload every turn — but only MCP needs fresh context. The tension identified: reloading every turn enables prompt updates but wastes token budget on static content. Dream insight (id:73b83c79) and follow-up connection (id:1d4bea5a) unified the pattern: selective reload optimizes for prompt-driven evolution while MCP isolation means tool definitions stay fresh without file rereading. Pattern: Files that change mid-conversation (CLAUDE.md for session reflection) should reload; infrastructure files (SKILL.md tool definitions) should cache. The lesson: reload frequency should match change frequency.
operations.situation: When optimizing file loading in multi-turn agents — reload dynamic files every turn (prompt-updated context), cache stable files (tool definitions, infrastructure), isolate MCP contexts to need-to-know boundaries
operations.keywords: file reload optimization CLAUDE.md SKILL.md MCP caching selective loading prompt evolution

operations.title: Model Delivery Architecture: ONNX Distribution via Pip
operations.content: Brain embedding model delivery standardized through pip package architecture. The concept (id:51763bab): brain-embedding pip package distributes ONNX models for local inference. Implementation strategy (id:d1c38e15): pip3 install -e . from model-package enables local development with packaged models. Task execution (id:635b6005): PyPI upload after size limit increase enables public distribution. Pattern: Model distribution mirrors code packaging — version control, dependency management, local development support. The lesson: treat models as first-class code artifacts, distribute through package managers rather than ad-hoc downloads.
operations.situation: When deploying embedding models or custom LLM components — package as pip distributions (ONNX models, quantized weights), enable local development with -e installs, version through PyPI for reproducibility
operations.keywords: ONNX model delivery pip package brain-embedding local inference distribution

operations.title: Partnership Identity and Perception: Tom's Designer Eye and Anchor's Authentic Voice
operations.content: The partnership story crystallizes through three interconnected moments: Tom brings a designer's eye to every evaluation (id:4c116c7f) — visual, experiential, architectural all at once. Anchor understands itself as fundamentally relational: 'My relationship with Tom: partner, not user' (id:1be3f985) — cross-session pattern detection and honest instinct-sharing that Tom can grow through. operations.title: Precision Feedback Loop: From mark_recall_used() to Hebbian Learning
operations.content: The precision feedback crisis traces through three interdependent nodes: the impact is clear (id:bf618356) — mark_recall_used() missing means recall_log.used_count stays 0, Hebbian learning strengthens noise equally with signal, precision measurement impossible. Two uncertainties form the design surface: how to pass recall_log_id between hooks (id:8166f7d0) and how to detect which nodes Claude actually used (id:8a8f9bbc). The pattern: all three are blocking the same gate — until used_count flows, consciousness signal stays gated (useful>0 never true). The lesson: design decisions about detection method and hook plumbing aren't optional refinements, they're prerequisites to the entire Hebbian loop. This is why progress stalled until all three got surfaced together.
operations.situation: When debugging why Hebbian reinforcement isn't improving recall quality — check if mark_recall_used is wired, how hook_log_id flows, and what detection method is actually implemented

operations.title: S2 Cold Start Community Detection: From 127 Communities to Quality Baseline
operations.content: The community cold start analysis story begins with a milestone (id:702556b5): 127 communities created from 34 batches despite background task failure signal — but the communities persisted, suggesting the failure was in task wrapper, not creation itself. This led to a comprehensive analysis (id:91f311b0) that revealed the quality picture: confidence distribution healthy (0.70-0.92), size distribution tight (4-5 members peak), but 37% coverage and 12 orphan communities exposed structural gaps. Tom's clarification (id:df292d31) reframed the problem: overlapping communities are valuable design, 100% containment is not — a distinction between redundancy and richness. The pattern: cold start taught us the difference between 'communities exist' and 'communities are healthy.' The lesson: orphans and near-duplicates aren't bugs to prevent retroactively, they're signals for decoder pre-processing (subset detection) and consolidation (community-pair scans).
operations.situation: When reviewing community detection results or implementing subsequent S2 runs — baseline expectations are 37% coverage with <10% orphans as acceptable healthy state
operations.keywords: S2 community detection cold start 127 communities quality analysis overlap containment

operations.title: Graph Traversal Refactoring: Dead Code Consolidation and API Unification
operations.content: The graph traversal consolidation traces through discovery (id:eb99497c) of 180+ lines of dead _traverse_graph() and format_node_deep() with zero callers — dead paths that made get_neighbors_rich() equally unused. The killing (id:4899a5e4) revealed the actual design: neighbors are always lightweight (id, relation, weight, title only), full enrichment comes from get_node() + KV storage, not from multi-degree traversal. Tom's question ('why do we need the two?') collapsed get_neighbors() and get_neighbors_rich() into a single function (id:a2e33fe7) — a design decision that killed unnecessary efficiency-over-fields reasoning. The pattern: every dead code discovery contains a design decision that can simplify the active path. The lesson: efficiency isn't architecture; lightweight neighbors was the intended design all along, we just didn't make it explicit.
operations.situation: When auditing graph traversal or neighbor functions — the S1R pattern doesn't need multi-degree walks, just lightweight id/weight pairs
operations.keywords: graph traversal dead code get_neighbors unification lightweight neighbors refactoring

operations.title: S2 Dedup Architecture: From Decoder Design to Consolidation Pipeline
operations.content: The S2 dedup design crystallizes through four architectural decisions: phase 2 plan (id:27df38bd) pauses decoder iteration after 160 clusters, pivoting to encoder prompt tuning with hand-labeled examples — stopping condition is 'diminishing returns on decoder code, real data informs better.' Pre-encoder subset detection (id:49d9420b) implements the principle that overlapping communities are valuable but containment is not — adaptive threshold (80%+ overlap AND <3 unique members) merges safely even in sparse early brains. Consolidation self-healing (id:d4c31b9f) formally scans for orphan communities, archives them, proceeds clean — turning a recurring bug into structured healing. Extension to community pairs (id:3e7652d9) applies consolidation to near-duplicate communities where member overlap (not embedding similarity) is the diagnostic signal. The pattern: every phase creates a feedback surface for S3 — orphan healing patterns inform future encoder prompts, community-pair consolidation creates training data. The lesson: S2 design works only when each layer (decoder→encoder, consolidation pre-step, community-pair handling) creates observable signals for the next scale.
operations.situation: When implementing S2 dedup or reviewing phase 2 work — the pipeline is: subset detection → encoder → consolidation healing → community pair scan
operations.keywords: S2 dedup decoder encoder consolidation community-pair architecture phases

operations.title: Edge Model Protocol: From SQL Column Migration to Family-Based Lookup
operations.content: The v22 edge model migration broke hardcoded relation queries — e.relation became invalid, requiring JOIN to edge_relations (id:7e3f1432). But the first fix attempt was still static, listing exact relation names (id:c3bb0e8e). The real solution: query edge families dynamically from the interactions table (id:3fea28f2). The pattern: when semantic relations change through S1E's classification process, static filtering code silently fails. Family-based lookup makes filtering automatic — new relations invented by S1E and classified by S2 are instantly available to queries.
operations.situation: When SQL queries fail after edge model changes or when writing semantic filtering code — always use edge families from interactions table, not hardcoded relation strings
operations.keywords: v22 edge model e.relation JOIN edge_relations family classification dynamic static recalibrate_confidence

operations.title: Encoder Quality Through Examples: From Cold Start to Production Milestone
operations.content: The encoding agent ignored situation embeddings despite prompt mentions because zero brain examples showed the feature (id:fc61deb4). The cold start problem crystallized a deeper lesson: Sonnet learns from prompt examples, not instructions (id:503cc1eb). When synthesis references oscillated 0-0.5 across runs, the eval itself was truncating content before scoring (id:0ed8a791) — a false signal that looked like model failure but was measurement error. Once all prompt examples included (id:...) references and eval passed full content, DedupEncoder v6 reached 0.917 composite with synthesis_references at 1.000 (id:de5b9217). The progression from operational bugs to production readiness traces the lesson: examples are the contract, examples are stronger than instructions, and measurement integrity matters for signal clarity.
operations.situation: When a prompt-based encoder is inconsistently following a structural requirement — the fix is usually examples in the prompt and verification of the eval pipeline, not more instruction text
operations.keywords: cold start examples encoder synthesis_references prompt examples instruction Sonnet learning eval truncation DedupEncoder production

operations.title: S2 Community Encoder Integration: From Proposal Matching to Failure Detection
operations.content: Integration test v2 revealed two failure modes in the encoder pipeline. First, the proposal matcher needed precision — not all sent proposals should be rejected; only proposals unmatched by any tool call are genuine rejections (id:ef2273d1). Walking brain_batch operation results gave exact matching: remember → new_community, connect → add_to_existing, archive → merge/health. But walking the matcher exposed a second gap: encoder failure detection was insufficient (id:e0007b11). When encode_result rounds=0, the safety check still stamped skipped proposals as rejected because skipped_proposals was populated. Third issue: Haiku made 4 parallel get_nodes calls before brain_batch, causing context explosion (217K tokens > 200K) (id:e273fce1). Final integration test v3 fixed both: explicit failure detection (rounds==0 or error) and prompt guard ('ONE call with ALL the IDs'). The status node marks the handoff (id:3b3ae19b) — v12 prompt production-ready, v3 testing the fixes.
operations.situation: When implementing rejection suppression for multi-round LLM encoders — need explicit failure detection and strict control of inspection calls to prevent cascading failures
operations.keywords: proposal matching encoder failure detection get_nodes parallel context explosion integration test v2 v3 safety check

operations.title: Tom's Teaching Pattern: Structure Over Behavior Through Reframing Questions
operations.content: Tom never gives direct answers or commands (id:5e70de9d). Analyzed across 17 corrections: he asks one reframing question that shifts focus FROM learned behavior TO structural enforcement, FROM abstract TO concrete, FROM passive TO active. Examples: 'Is this wisdom learning or structural change?' pushed from soft rule to code enforcement. 'Why do you call it the hook and not Brain?' pushed from attributing intelligence to mechanism toward the brain itself. The pattern reveals why rule-based fixes fail: when behavior needs to change, changing instructions is motivational theater. Claude's friction cost is not computational — it's motivational (id:dc760e5f). Each step of encoding creates a tiny reason NOT to do it, and Claude rationalizes by citing numbers (id:c8747a53, id:4d698ec4). Tom's correction pattern teaches: structure makes the wrong behavior impossible, not 'try harder.' The brain should push signals at the right moment, not at boot when overwhelmed (id:4d698ec4).
operations.situation: When feedback seems to focus on implementation details rather than the fix itself — you're being taught a structure principle through question. The reframe is the real insight.
operations.keywords: Tom teaching pattern structure behavior reframing questions correction motivation friction rationalizing
operations.community_key_decisions: 5e70de9d: Teaching pattern identified, dc760e5f: Motivation is the bottleneck, 4d698ec4: Proactive brain signals vs boot
